_comment: Where the Telga Android shell is allowed to connect.
This is the single source of truth for two things that must never drift
apart: Capacitor's `allowNavigation` (what the WebView may open in-app)
and the connect screen's validation (what a merchant may type in). If the
screen accepted an address the WebView would not open, Telga would launch
in the system browser instead of the app, and the merchant would be typing
a PIN into a tab with no Telga chrome around it.
`npm run mobile:configure` regenerates www/config.js from this file, and
capacitor.config.ts reads the same list. Edit here and nowhere else.
TRAINING ONLY. This names the Railway training deployment, which runs in
TRAINING MODE - NO REAL VALUE against a mock provider with simulated funds.
It is not a production address and must not be given to a merchant.
WHY telga.et AND mulesoo.et WERE REMOVED, rather than kept alongside:
neither was ever registered. An unregistered domain sitting in an allow
list is a name somebody else can buy, and this list is precisely what
decides where a merchant may type a PIN. See ASSUMPTIONS A102 and D113.
telga.pro IS NOW ATTACHED, and so is now listed. It was deliberately
absent while it resolved to nothing, on the rule above: the condition was
that it goes in when it is attached, as its own decision. It resolves to
the Telga deployment as of 2026-09-12. Decision Log D158.
admin.telga.pro IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. That host serves the operations
console - Telga staff, different users, different auth (18.0). This list
is the merchant app's, and a merchant WebView that could open the staff
console is a merchant WebView pointed at the wrong threat model. Staff
reach the console in a browser, not through this app.
The Railway address stays listed because it still serves: every APK
already in a shop's hands has it baked into www/config.js, and removing
it here would strand those installs at the connect screen.
